title: Independent Medical Travel Advisor vs Commission Agency: Why It Matters
seoTitle: Independent Medical Travel Advisor vs Commission Agency
metaDescription: Learn how free medical tourism agencies earn clinic commissions and why Itinerary of Türkiye's flat-fee advisory keeps your clinic shortlist unbiased.
quickAnswer: An independent medical travel advisor in Türkiye charges you a transparent flat fee and accepts zero clinic commissions. In contrast, "free" medical tourism agencies earn referral kickbacks from partner clinics, which narrows your options to providers willing to pay marketing fees rather than those best matched to your priorities.
category: Medical Travel to Türkiye — Independent Advisory & Safety (The ITO Standard)

body.text: How do "free" medical tourism agencies make money from clinics?

"Free" medical tourism agencies generate revenue by collecting referral commissions—often structured as a percentage of your procedure bill or a flat per-patient bounty—directly from the clinics they promote. Because the clinic pays the broker out of its operating margin, the agency's commercial client is the clinic, not the traveling patient.

When a coordinator tells you their planning service costs nothing, that fee is already folded into the clinic's quote. High-volume marketing brokers sign commercial agreements with specific dental centers, hair-transplant studios, or cosmetic clinics in Istanbul and Antalya. In return for sending confirmed bookings, the agency receives a payout once you arrive and pay.

As the [UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) Turkey health guidance](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/turkey/health) warns, private companies have a direct financial interest in booking your treatment, so their marketing material should never be your sole source of information. Before trusting any intermediary, verify that both the facility and any licensed facilitator hold valid authorization listed by the [Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Health](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html).
Why does a commission model create conflict of interest in clinic selection?

A commission model creates a structural conflict of interest because the agency only gets paid when you book through its contracted network. Advisors working on commission have a financial incentive to steer you toward clinics offering the highest referral percentage, fastest slot availability, or bundled hotel markups rather than independent hospital standards.
This incentive gap affects every stage of your trip:

items: Narrowed shortlists: Reputable hospitals and specialist surgeons who do not pay third-party referral fees are routinely omitted from commission-agency quotes.

Pressure to book fast: Sales agents paid on monthly conversion targets push flash deposits and short decision windows, contradicting [NHS cosmetic surgery abroad guidance](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/cosmetic-procedures/advice/cosmetic-surgery-abroad/) that recommends two consultations and a cooling-off period.
Bundled hotel markups: "All-inclusive" packages frequently pair clinics with distant, low-cost hotels that pay extra kickbacks rather than quiet properties near your hospital.

body.text: How does Itinerary of Türkiye's client-paid flat fee keep advice unbiased?

[Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/about) operates on a strict client-paid flat fee run directly by its two founders in Türkiye: paid by our clients, independent of provider commissions. Because we accept no kickbacks from hospitals, clinics, hotels, or transfer companies, we have zero financial stake in which provider you choose—or whether you postpone treatment.

Our [medical tourism advisory service](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/services/medical-tourism) focuses on practical ground realities that commission brokers gloss over. We help you verify Ministry of Health authorization status, map realistic recovery logistics between your clinic and hotel, and spot common [medical tourism red flags in Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/medical-tourism-red-flags-turkey) before you wire a deposit.
Use this quick checklist before hiring any advisor in Türkiye:

items: Ask in writing whether they receive any commission, marketing fee, or discount kickback from clinics or hotels.
Confirm you will receive itemized, direct invoices from the hospital rather than an opaque package price.
Verify that the advisor works directly with you on logistics without pressuring you into a specific surgeon.
Prepare a clear list of [questions to ask a Turkish clinic before paying any deposit](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/questions-to-ask-clinic-turkey).

body.text: What remains strictly your licensed medical team's clinical decision?

Every medical judgment—including diagnosis, procedure eligibility, surgical technique, anesthesia plan, prescriptions, and fitness-to-fly clearance—belongs exclusively to your licensed physicians and hospital team. An independent medical travel advisor coordinates non-clinical logistics such as scheduling, neighborhood selection, transfers, and companion planning, and never intervenes in medical care.
We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions.

Both the [NHS](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/cosmetic-procedures/advice/cosmetic-surgery-abroad/) and the [Australian Smartraveller medical tourism advisory](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/travel-essentials/travel-health/medical-tourism) emphasize discussing your procedure with your home doctor first and consulting directly with the operating surgeon rather than relying on sales staff. We never diagnose conditions, recommend surgical methods, or guarantee clinical outcomes.

If you want unbiased ground support for an upcoming trip to Türkiye, reach out to our founders via our [medical tourism services page](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/services/medical-tourism). Please do not share passport or ID scans, medical records, or payment details in your first enquiry.

faq.q: How much do commission agencies typically take from Turkish clinics?
faq.a: Referral commissions vary by procedure and provider, but agencies commonly take a percentage of the treatment price or a per-patient referral fee built into the clinic's international pricing.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye accept discounts or perks from Istanbul hotels or clinics?
faq.a: No. Itinerary of Türkiye is funded solely by our client-paid flat fee. We are paid by our clients and remain independent of provider commissions.

faq.q: Can an independent advisor still help if I already chose my hospital?
faq.a: Yes. Many clients already have a hospital or surgeon in mind and hire us strictly for recovery hotel selection, private transfers, companion itineraries, and realistic travel sequencing.

faq.q: Will Itinerary of Türkiye review my medical scans or tell me which procedure I need?
faq.a: No. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions, including reviewing scans, assessing candidacy, and setting post-operative restrictions.

faq.q: How can I check if a Turkish clinic is legally authorized for international patients?
faq.a: Look up the facility on the [Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Health](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html) international health tourism authorization portal before paying any deposit.

faq.q: Is a flat-fee advisor more expensive than a "free" agency?
faq.a: Often it costs less overall, because you avoid inflated commission-padded package quotes, pay hospitals directly, and make informed choices without sales pressure.
